# Exercise 2.1 — Colour play

```{=typst}
#align(center)[
  #text(size: 24pt, fill: rgb("#6a0dad"), weight: "bold")[Jane Trainer]
]
```

# Exercise 2.2 — Show rule for strong text

```{=typst}
#show strong: it => smallcaps(it)
```

**This bold sentence is now rendered in small caps.** Every bold passage
after the show rule is transformed the same way.

# Exercise 2.3 — Warning box

```{=typst}
#block(
  fill: rgb("#fdecea"),
  stroke: (left: 3pt + rgb("#c0392b")),
  inset: 10pt,
  radius: 4pt,
  width: 100%,
)[
  *Warning.* Raw Typst is powerful, but scattering it through a document
  makes maintenance hard. Prefer set/show rules near the top — or better,
  a shared template (Module 4).
]
```

# Exercise 2.4 — Data-driven Typst

```{r}
#| echo: fenced
#| output: asis
m <- round(mean(iris$Sepal.Length), 2)

cat("```{=typst}\n",
    "#align(center)[",
    "#block(fill: rgb(\"#eef6f8\"), inset: 12pt, radius: 6pt)[",
    "#text(size: 20pt, weight: \"bold\")[", m, " cm]\n\n",
    "Mean sepal length across all 150 iris flowers",
    "]]\n",
    "```", sep = "")
```
